newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-LEONARDO COMPLETES SWITCH FROM DEFENCE TO ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEONARDO COMPLETES SWITCH FROM DEFENCE TO ATTACK.

text.p: A 10-year transformation from defender to attacker will be completed on Wednesday when Brazil's Leonardo starts at forward for Paris St Germain in the European Cup Winners' Cup final.
Leonardo Nascimento de Aruajo first plied his trade at left back for Flamengo as a 17-year-old.
"At 17 when you're offered a place in the first team you'll play anywhere," he recalled in an interview.
Leonardo made his international debut in 1989 but it was not until after Brazil won the 1994 World Cup in the United States that he got a chance to switch to his preferred slot.
"I told the coach (Mario Zagallo) that I wanted to play in midfield and a former player he understood and gave me a chance," said Leonardo.
That chance came in a friendly against Spain in Valencia, where Leonardo had spent two seasons from 1991 to 1993 and where he picked up another of his four languages.
"It wasn't easy to change, it was a challenge for me," he said. "But I'm very happy now."
Leonardo, having consolidated his place in the Brazil side preparing to defend the World Cup in France next year, will start up front for Paris St Germain against Barcelona in Rotterdam on Wednesday.
He sees it, however, as a natural consequence of his time in Japan where he played for Kashima Antlers and had a free-roving role in the midfield.
"That was a fantastic experience, participating in a lot of different things in only the second year of professionalism there," the Rio de Janiero-born Leonardo said.

However, his desire to secure a berth in Brazil's 1998 World Cup side remained an overriding priority and when an offer from Paris St Germain came with four months still left on his contract with Kashima, he left having put them on course for the title.
At PSG, Leonardo has linked up with his former Sao Paulo team mate Rai and Brazil's former captain Ricardo, now the manager at the Parisian club.
"They came for me and I saw it as a challenge to play in Europe again," he said.
Leonardo, who joined Sao Paulo from Flamengo in 1990 and went on to win the Brazilian, South American and world club title beating AC Milan in the Tokyo final in 1991, has had a mixed season at PSG.

Having helped his new club notch up a run of 13 games without defeat from the first day of the league championship, his commitment when the going got tough was questioned as PSG plunged into a mid-season crisis.

He did, however, come back from international duty with Brazil in October to inspire PSG to a 4-0 home win over Galatasaray in the Cup Winners' Cup second round after missing the 4-2 first leg defeat in Turkey.

Leonardo was nursing an injury when PSG crashed 6-1 at home to Juventus in the first leg of the European Super Cup in January, coming off the bench in the second half when the match had already been settled.
Results in the league went badly and his goals dried up. Having scored seven in the first 13 games to early October, he has not scored again in the league.
His goal against Liverpool in the first leg of the Cup Winners' Cup semifinal, a 3-0 win in Paris, was his third in the competition but first for PSG since October despite moving further upfield.
The balance of the team, however, has improved and others, striker Patrice Loko in particular, play off him.
Leonardo will be particularly keen to make an impact in France next year after missing the 1994 final because of a four-match suspension.
He incurred the heaviest penalty ever handed out at a finals when he elbowed Tad Ramos in the head during a second-round match, fracturing the American's skull.
